France: Students call for school blockades starting Monday
 France France: Students call for school blockades starting Monday
 Pierre Sourzat considers the government's announcements insufficient. Other organizations plan blockades on Tuesday and Thursday, following two weeks of school holidays.
 Education By Anne Sophie 
 · 01/11/26 · 2 min

Français (Bénin) 
 The movement Les Lycéens ! is calling for high school blockades across France to resume on Monday, November 2, the day students return from the All Saints’ holiday. Its president, Pierre Sourzat, announced this on Sunday during an interview with RMC, contesting the notion that the government’s measures adequately address students’ demands.
 Sourzat anticipates blockades at certain schools starting Monday, followed by a larger mobilization on Tuesday. The Union of High School Students and the Student Union have also called for blockades at high schools and universities on Tuesday, November 3, and Thursday, November 5, coinciding with a nationwide strike.
 Earlier this week, the government announced several measures aimed at addressing the protests that have been ongoing for six weeks. These include the gradual replacement of Parcoursup by 2028 and funding for the renovation of school buildings. The government also announced a cap of 28 students per second-year class and the creation of 15,000 new places in higher education.
 Pierre Sourzat believes that the reform of post-baccalaureate admissions does not sufficiently address the shortage of places in higher education. He is also calling for a reduction in class sizes across all grades, not just in second year. Emmanuel Macron, for his part, urged on Thursday for classes to resume peacefully, asserting that the youth’s demands had been heard.
 When asked about the duration of the mobilization, the president of Les Lycéens ! did not set an end date. He stated that it would depend on the government’s response, while acknowledging that the blockades could lead to academic delays for the participating students.
